Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- from the date of accident till its realization for the fatal injury sustained by Sh. Ganesh Yadav, aged about 52 years in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 08.07.2020 at about 9:30 PM in front of Triveni Colony, Bakhtawarpur Road, MACP No. 203/20;
FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025 Delhi, involving Truck bearing registration no.
DL1LW-9617 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.
2.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 08.07.2020, deceased Sh. Ganesh Yadav was going to his place on his rickshaw At about 9:30 PM, when he reached in front of Triveni Colony, Bakhtawarpur Road, Delhi, offending vehicle i.e., Truck bearing registration no. DL1LW-9617 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high, in a rash and negligent manner and in a zigzag manner, came and hit against the aforesaid rickshaw with a great force, as a result of which, deceased sustained serious injuries.

He was immediately taken to BJRM Hospital and thereafter, concerned doctors referred him to RML Hospital and during treatment, he succumbed to the injuries suffered by him in the accident in question.
His postmortem was conducted at RML Hospital.
A case U/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS. Alipur vide FIR No. 292/2020 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.

sentences.text: In their joint written statement, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e., driver and registered owner claimed that alleged accident was not caused by respondent no. 1.
It is further claimed that respondent no. 1 was having valid DL, Fitness, Insurance and RC on the date of accident.
It is also claimed that alleged offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident.

4. In its Written Statement, the respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company has claimed that accident in question occurred due to sole negligence of deceased and thus, it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
It has been admitted that offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

The careful perusal of testimony of aforesaid witness i.e. PW2 would go to show that the respondents more particularly insurance company have not been able to impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination despite he being cross-examined at length by counsel for insurance company.
It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 292/20 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Alipur with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on 09.07.2020 (accident being caused on 08.07.2020 at 9:30 pm) on the basis of statement of complainant Sh. Dinesh Singh who specifically told the registration number of offending vehicle as DL1LW-9617 in his statement.
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.

Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no.
1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.
MACP No. 203/20; FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025

Moreover, the presence of PW2 at the spot of accident at the time of accident is substantiated by the fact that he joined the investigation with IO and gave statement as a eyewitness and by seeing the list of witnesses annexed alongwith the chargesheet filed in the criminal case shows his name mentioned at S.No. 2.
On the other hand, respondents have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW2 in this regard during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by PW2 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

11. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022

that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair Bindu Devi And Ors vs Krishan Kumar on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92076935/

17. It has been duly established as per findings of issue no.1 that deceased Sh. Ganesh Yadav had sustained fatal injury in the accident in question on 08.07.2020 at about 9:30 PM in front of Triveni Colony, Bakhtawarpur Road, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
Accordingly, claimant(s) are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

18. The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.

It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.

Justice and justness emanate MACP No. 203/20; FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025 from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
19.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.

sentences.text: Hereinafter, assessment is divided into several criteria, as applicable to the facts of the present case.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 20.

PW1 Smt. Bindu has deposed in her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A that deceased was aged about 50 years; he was working as a Rickshaw Puller and was earning Rs. 1,000/- per day at the time of MACP No. 203/20; FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025 accident.
She further deposed that all the petitioners were fully dependent upon the income of deceased and had no other source of income.

She has relied upon DAR Ex. PW1/1(colly) and claim petition Ex. PW1/2(colly).
21.
During her cross examination on behalf of insurance company, she deposed that her son Abhinandan was working as a Labour and earning Rs. 400/- daily.
She further deposed that Abhinandan was married.
She further deposed that her son namely Niwas Yadav was also working as a Labour and he was also earning Rs. 400/- daily.
She further deposed that Niwas was also married.
She denied the suggestion that her husband was not earning Rs. 1,000/- per day.
She further denied the suggestion that Salita Devi was not her daughter.
Counsel for petitioners argued that minimum wages of Delhi should be taken for computation of income under this head as deceased was working and earning in Delhi at the time of accident.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for insurance company argued that minimum wages of Bihar should be taken as deceased was permanent resident of Bihar.

23. As already noted above, PW1 Smt. Bindu Devi, who is widow of deceased deposed in her evidence that deceased was working as Rickshaw Puller and was earning Rs. 1,000/- per day at the time of accident.

Apart from the bald statement made by PW1 that deceased was earning Rs. 1,000/-
per MACP No. 203/20; FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025 day
, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove the monthly income of deceased at the time of accident in question.
Petitioners have also failed to file any educational qualification documents of deceased.
24. It is relevant to note here that petitioners have claimed in the claim petition that deceased was Rickshaw Puller in Delhi and was earning Rs. 1,000/- per day at the time of accident.

Although, the petitioners have failed to lead any cogent evidence in this regard but the said fact is duly substantiated from the copy of FIR wherein it is specifically mentioned that the accident had taken place when the deceased was plying rickshaw in the area Bakhtawarpur Road, Alipur, Delhi, which was hit by the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

It is not out of place to mention here that though, the petitioners have failed to file any documentary proof with regard to working and earning of deceased in Delhi at the time of accident but it can be presumed that a person who is permanent resident of Bihar would not come to Delhi with Rickshaw on daily basis for plying the same.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am inclined to take the minimum wages of an unskilled person as per Minimum Wages Act applicable in the State of Delhi during the period in question in order to compute the loss of dependency.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 15,310/- per month during the relevant period.
The accident in question had occurred on 08.07.2020.

sentences.text: It is stated that the deceased was survived by four dependents i.e. widow and three major children of deceased.
However, Ld. Counsel for insurance company argued that petitioners were not dependent upon the deceased at the time of accident.

During cross-examination of PW1 (widow of deceased), she deposed that her sons namely Abhinandan and Niwas were labour and earning Rs.
400/- per day.
However, it is not clear as to both the sons of deceased were working as labour and earning at the time of accident or not.
Even otherwise, no suggestion has been put to the witness regarding non-dependency of her minor sons upon the deceased at the time of accident.
In view of the aforesaid and considering all the facts and circumstances, it is held that there were four dependents i.e. widow and three children of deceased at the time of accident.
Hence, there has to be deduction of one MACP No. 203/20; FIR No. 292/20; PS. Alipur DOD: 05.08.2025 fourth as held in the case of Sarla Verma mentioned supra.
Thus, the total of loss of dependency would come out to Rs. 16,67,259/- (Rs. 15,310/- X 3/4 X 110/100 X 12 X 11).
Hence, a sum of Rs. 16,67,259/- is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 27.

In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as, Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Tribunal considers that all the petitioners are entitled for payment of Rs. 40,000/- each towards "loss of consortium".

By way of pronouncement of Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has been pleased to hold that there shall be an increase of 10% on account of 'inflation' after a period of three years.

Applying, the afore-cited binding law the The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Ltd. V. LR's of Sukhbir Singh, MAC. APP. 518/2013 vide judgment pronounced on 13.07.2023 has been pleased to direct the entitlement of dependents to 10% increase under this head, though, the date of accident was of 2011 and the date of impugned award was of 2013.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on 09.07.2020 (accident being caused on 08.07.2020 at 9:30 pm) on the basis of statement of complainant Sh. Dinesh Singh who specifically told the registration number of offending vehicle as DL1LW-9617 in his statement.
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no.
1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.
Moreover, the presence of PW2 at the spot of accident at the time of accident is substantiated by the fact that he joined the investigation with IO and gave statement as a eyewitness and by seeing the list of witnesses annexed alongwith the chargesheet filed in the criminal case shows his name mentioned at S.No. 2.

10. Counsel for petitioners argued that minimum wages of Delhi should be taken for computation of income under this head as deceased was working and earning in Delhi at the time of accident.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for insurance company argued that minimum wages of Bihar should be taken as deceased was permanent resident of Bihar.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the other hand, respondents have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW2 in this regard during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by PW2 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.
All the injuries were ante-mortem in nature.
